chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, who said:
Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: "The salat of supererogatory devotion is like a gift: whenever it is brought, it is accepted. So advance of it whatever you wish, and delay of it whatever you wish."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The proper understanding of these reports is that they constitute a concession for one whose condition is known to be such that, if he does not perform them earlier, he will become occupied away from them and will not be able to make them up. But when excuses are absent, then it is not permissible to advance them, according to what we have explained. What indicates what we have said is what he narrated:

key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a legal concession granted due to circumstance
key_terms.صَلَاةُ ٱلتَّطَوُّعِ: supererogatory salat performed voluntarily beyond the obligatory prayers
key_terms.قَضَائِهَا: making it up after its time
key_terms.ٱلْهَدِيَّةِ: a gift, used here as a comparison for something accepted whenever offered

ai.seo_question: Can supererogatory salat be performed earlier or later than its usual time?
ai.summary: This report states that supererogatory salat has a flexible time, likening it to a gift that is accepted whenever it is offered. Shaykh al-Tusi then explains that this flexibility is understood as a concession for one who fears missing it due to circumstances, not a general permission without excuse.
